label: canon-c19-e0ai500-n2
_why: THE LOOP'S THIRD PICK (2026-09-15; the standing loop: report -> clock -> the best NEW config). The found configuration is canon-c19-in12 (F117: GDP 1.09 / 1.07x vanilla, workers per capita 0.65 / 0.67x, rung 0 out-earned at 22-26% vs 44-54%) and its one unmet goal is rung 0's DEATH: it thins to 45% staffing but its LEVEL COUNT grows in every book of the sweep (649 at 1840 -> 1,568-1,672 at 1935 at C 1.9; 1,889 at C 1.6; 2,554 under the x1.3 lift) - the AI keeps BUILDING the old rung (the company rebuild, F97 s4) while it out-earns nothing. Both price levers tried on it failed: the x1.3 input lift at C 1.9 removed the dip and RAN AWAY (F118, 1.44x), and on the 2.05 slope it stalled (session 20260915_033205: 0.72 / 0.71 / 0.72 / 0.70x at 1890-1920). So this book leaves every price alone and turns the one willingness lever the design has for this: rung 0's ai_value (the AI's construction desire) HALVED to 500, e1-e3 unchanged at 3,000 / 9,000 / 27,000 (make_ab_config --ai-ladder 500,3000,9000,27000 in place of --ai-steep <17>:3). Everything else as canon-c19-in12 (cost 1.9^era, the x1.2 lift, A 2.2 / B 1.5, divisor 0.000125, the defines, the 24-month bar). One lever. A willingness lever, not a block (the no-artificial-limits rule): rung 0 stays buildable, less wanted. Expected: fewer new rung-0 levels, so its staffed share falls as old levels close and the frontier absorbs the labour, with little new push on the capital price - the runaway needs cheap frontier capital, which this does not change.
